segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus took three of his closest friends — Peter, James, and John — up a high mountain, away from everyone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there, in front of them, he changed. His clothes turned a blinding white, brighter than anything on earth, and for one moment they saw him shining with who he really is.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Two of the greatest prophets, Moses and Elias, appeared and stood talking with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter, overwhelmed, blurted out the first thing that came to him.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He wanted to keep the moment. Build something, stay a while. Mark adds, kindly, that Peter did not know what to say, because they were so afraid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a bright cloud settled over the mountain, and out of it came a voice.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: This is my beloved Son: hear him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This is my Son, whom I love. Listen to him. Not build for him. Not stay up here with him. Listen to him. Of everything the Father could have said on that mountain, he gave them one sentence and one instruction.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And then it was over. The light faded, the cloud lifted, and Jesus stood there alone — the same gentle friend, reaching down to lift them up. Do not be afraid, he told them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For one moment they saw who he really is — and heaven said, hear him. That invitation still stands.
